body: We would really need some working code for this... If jsfiddle doesn't wok, maybe you can create a isolatest test, zip it and share it on dropbox?
@electricessence Please see "How to report a bug" in the [guidelines](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md).

I understand how this should have been reported, but like I said, I spent about two full work days trying to figure out if it was even a bug or not.  You can take ANY existing THREE.js boiler plate and paste it this into it and reordering the renderDepth does nothing.  The issue with jsFiddle is that adding dat.gui as a reference breaks and nothing shows up.

As you see in the example, setting the renderDepth in reverse should cause a reverse order, but it does not.

Here is a working sample (no dat.gui) that you can fork and simply rearrange renderDepth in whatever values you like:
http://jsfiddle.net/electricessence/QHssJ/1/

Just so you understand my intention with using renderDepth.
What I really want is a way to easily custom sort (reorder after the original sort occurs) the view's z-order.  Not only do I want to be able to have a single object within a scene render below or above another, I want to be able to have entire groups of objects to be rendered in a different order within the global space.
https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/issues/5500

I tried hacking with the sorting mechanism in the three.js file, but nothing worked.  Trying to reverse sort the opaque objects did nothing.  It may have been where I inserted my code, but I feel like there' something going on that I'm not aware of.

> I understand how this should have been reported, but like I said, I spent about two full work days trying to figure out if it was even a bug or not. 

We ask for working code so we can be of help. We ask that of everyone, regardless of how much time they have spent so far.

In your fiddle, set your materials to be transparent with `opacity` 0.5 and you will see the `renderDepth` settings taking effect.

> You can take ANY existing THREE.js boiler plate and paste it this into it and reordering the renderDepth does nothing.

I understand it may seem that it takes no time to paste some code in a boiler plate. But consider a near future where maybe 100 persons per day expect us to do just that. At the end of that day we wouldn't have time to develop the library, we would have just spent the day pasting code from people into a boiler plate and figuring out what's going on.

The easier you can make it for us to help the better. So, thanks for taking the time to put together the jsfiddle.

It indeed looks like is not behaving as it should. Adding `depthTest: false` should do the trick but doesn't seem to be doing anything. I'll take a closer look.

> It indeed looks like it is not behaving as it should.

I do not see a problem here. A scene of opaque objects should render the same, regardless of the `renderDepth` settings -- at longs as `depthTest` and `depthWrite` are at their default values.
As I said, I tried to change `depthTest` to `false` and `renderDepth` didn't seem to be working. I didn't look at it closely though.
Here is a fiddle with a little more light on the subject: http://jsfiddle.net/QHssJ/2/.

Thanks guys.  Using your link above, I changed the material opacity in the constructor and I'm not seeing any difference:
http://jsfiddle.net/electricessence/9krxa9tq/

You say that renderDepth doesn't matter for opaque objects?  I couldn't find any documentation or answered questions so I assumed renderDepth was a sorting order override from what I read, regardless of opacity.
Ok, confirmed. I broke `renderDepth` O:)

issue.title: Bug or bad behaviour with camera big coordinates confirmed
issue.body:
This can be checked using the editor. 
You have to create a simple box, move it to 200000, 4000000 and test some ray-intersects.

To make it simple you can add some lines to editor code. 
1.- add  inside  viewport.js>  handleClick a global reference to the object clicked.
      ....if ( intersects.length > 0 ) {
      var object = intersects[ 0 ].object;
      global_object = object;
2.- Inside toolbar.js , below scale button (for example)  add
    var center = new UI.Button( 'center last ' ).onClick( function () 
    { signals.objectFocused.dispatch( global_object );  } );
    buttons.add( center );

(so, you can move an object and center the camera on it )

Ok, Now start a new scene. 
Add a box, click it (now you have a reference to it as a 'global object' and you can 'center the view on it' .(using the 'center' button added) 
Move the box to 200000 4000000, (the utm coords of any place in the world)
Click on 'center' and play with the zoom until you view the box.
Change  & play with the camera position using the mouse  and make some clicks and you discover that you can't  select the box as easy as you expected.
it is as if the mouse really was at other point than expected. 
So I think there is a problem with the unproject vector  matrix precission or something related.
Maybe the vector (xx,yy, 0.5) can be the reason ?  

If not , why is this happen. ?
Thanks.

body: Working on a fairly large three.js project, but haven't updated to a version impacted by this yet. Is there no way to control the `renderDepth` at all anymore? I rely on it quite heavily :(
Hmmm... I'm considering different approaches. So far, having a custom sort pass in the renderer sounds like the best solution but I haven't thought about usability yet.
@mrdoob, whatever you do, be sure to allow for referencing the original order.
How so?
Is this still on the radar? Would love to see renderDepth return for r70!
Yeah, it would indeed be great if `renderDepth` issues would be solved in r70

Another vote for fixing this.

I use renderDepth for my sky systems (so a couple of large planes, existing at same height, with clouds rendered via a shader). For now I will rolling this into a single plane to get around this change.

There's also other various tricks used in games that require the the ability to set or force render depth values.

@Cubiverse There appears to be a lot of confusion about what is possible -- or should be possible -- when "setting `renderDepth`" in three.js. It would be helpful if you would provide a live link to demonstrate your use case, and explain exactly what you believe should be happening that is not.

Are you interested in setting a custom `renderDepth` so an object will be rendered "in front" when it is not, or so an object will be rendered _correctly_, when it is not?

> There's also other various tricks used in games that require the the ability to set or force render depth values.

Which ones are you referring to?
